#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Delete old CI pre-releases of one repository through the GitHub API (TS-608),
# which also removes their release assets. Git tags
# stay. CI pre-releases are the ci-<sha>-run-<id> and
# image-<sha>-run-<id>-attempt-<n> releases; every other release is left alone.
#
# usage: prune-releases.sh REPOSITORY PINS
#   REPOSITORY  owner/name, e.g. TerraScale/ts-orchestrator
#   PINS        file of pinned source revisions (40 hex), binary digests
#               (64 hex) and release tags, separated by any whitespace or
#               JSON; it must name at least one pin
#
# Kept: the newest TS_PRUNE_KEEP (default 20) CI pre-releases, any published in
# the last TS_PRUNE_KEEP_DAYS (default 7) days, and any release whose tag
# names a pinned revision or tag, or whose small manifests (*.json, *.sha256,
# SHA256SUMS) name a pinned digest. A manifest that cannot be read keeps its
# release. TS_PRUNE_DRY_RUN=true only logs. Environment: GH_TOKEN,
# which may delete the repository's releases.
set -euo pipefail

fail() { echo "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 2 ]] || { echo "usage: $0 REPOSITORY PINS" >&2; exit 2; }
repository=$1 pins_file=$2
[[ $repository =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "invalid repository $repository"
: "${GH_TOKEN:?GitHub token is required}"
export GH_HOST=github.com
keep=${TS_PRUNE_KEEP:-20} keep_days=${TS_PRUNE_KEEP_DAYS:-7} dry_run=${TS_PRUNE_DRY_RUN:-false}
[[ $keep =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $keep_days =~ ^[0-9]+$ && $dry_run =~ ^(true|false)$ ]] ||
	fail 'TS_PRUNE_KEEP and TS_PRUNE_KEEP_DAYS must be numbers, TS_PRUNE_DRY_RUN true or false'

# A pin is any revision, digest or CI tag in the file: the same words whether
# it is fleet-status JSON or a plain list.
mapfile -t pins < <(grep -oE '\b((ci|image)-[0-9a-f]{40}-run-[0-9]+(-attempt-[0-9]+)?|[0-9a-f]{64}|[0-9a-f]{40})\b' \
	"$pins_file" | sort -u)
((${#pins[@]} > 0)) || fail "$pins_file names no pin; refusing to prune without the live releases"
declare -A pinned
for pin in "${pins[@]}"; do pinned[$pin]=1; done
echo "pins: ${pins[*]}"

umask 077
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
echo '[]' > "$work/releases.json"
for ((page = 1; ; page++)); do
	gh api "repos/$repository/releases?per_page=50&page=$page" > "$work/page.json"
	[[ $(jq length "$work/page.json") == 0 ]] && break
	jq -s 'add' "$work/releases.json" "$work/page.json" > "$work/all.json"
	mv "$work/all.json" "$work/releases.json"
done

cutoff=$(date -u -d "-$keep_days days" +%s)
# Candidates: CI pre-releases past the newest $keep and older than the cutoff.
jq -c --argjson keep "$keep" --argjson cutoff "$cutoff" '
	[.[] | select(.prerelease and (.draft | not) and (.tag_name | test("^(ci|image)-[0-9a-f]{40}-run-[0-9]+(-attempt-[0-9]+)?$")))]
	| sort_by(.published_at) | reverse | .[$keep:][]
	| select((.published_at | fromdateiso8601) < $cutoff)
	| {id, tag: .tag_name, published_at, bytes: ([.assets[].size] | add // 0),
		manifests: [.assets[] | select((.name | test("(\\.json|\\.sha256|^SHA256SUMS)$")) and .size <= 1048576)
			| .name]}' "$work/releases.json" > "$work/candidates.json"

# names_pin TAG MANIFEST_NAME...: whether the release is pinned; an unreadable
# manifest counts as pinned.
names_pin() {
	local tag=$1 name word
	shift
	[[ -n ${pinned[$tag]:-} || -n ${pinned[$(cut -d- -f2 <<< "$tag")]:-} ]] && return 0
	for name in "$@"; do
		rm -f -- "$work/manifest"
		gh release download "$tag" --repo "$repository" --pattern "$name" --output "$work/manifest" || { echo "kept $tag: cannot read $name" >&2; return 0; }
		for word in $(grep -oE '\b[0-9a-f]{64}\b' "$work/manifest" || true); do
			[[ -n ${pinned[$word]:-} ]] && return 0
		done
	done
	return 1
}

deleted=0 freed=0 kept=0
while IFS= read -r release; do
	tag=$(jq -r .tag <<< "$release")
	mapfile -t manifests < <(jq -r '.manifests[]' <<< "$release")
	if names_pin "$tag" "${manifests[@]}"; then
		echo "kept $tag: pinned"
		kept=$((kept + 1))
		continue
	fi
	bytes=$(jq -r .bytes <<< "$release")
	if [[ $dry_run == false ]]; then
		gh api --method DELETE "repos/$repository/releases/$(jq -r .id <<< "$release")"
	fi
	echo "deleted $tag published=$(jq -r .published_at <<< "$release") bytes=$bytes dry_run=$dry_run"
	deleted=$((deleted + 1)) freed=$((freed + bytes))
done < "$work/candidates.json"
printf 'TS_RELEASE_PRUNE repository=%s releases=%s deleted=%s kept_pinned=%s bytes=%s dry_run=%s\n' \
	"$repository" "$(jq length "$work/releases.json")" "$deleted" "$kept" "$freed" "$dry_run"

//go:embed race-test.sh
var raceScript []byte

//go:embed race-durations.txt
var committedDurations []byte

var schedulerLabs = []string{
	"TestLabTLSHostSessionFencesAndRestartsAfterControllerLoss",
	"TestControllerThreeProcessBootstrapAndRestart",
	"TestLabTLSHostSessionRecoversAfterBlackholedController",
	"TestLabTLSHostSessionRecoversAfterControllerLoss",
	"TestAuthenticatedOperatorToHostDeliveryWithControllerLoss",
}

const solo = "TestOfflineReadbackMismatchDiscardsCandidate"

// noraceTest is the fixture test estimated as norace.
const noraceTest = "TestRetry"

// The fixture estimates make cost order differ from name order: round-robin
// by name would pair TestThree with TestFail and TestOne with Example.
const fixtureDurations = `# fixture estimates
rest - 5
./internal/app TestLabTLSHostSessionFencesAndRestartsAfterControllerLoss 95/1 idle
./internal/app TestControllerThreeProcessBootstrapAndRestart 80/1 idle
./internal/app TestLabTLSHostSessionRecoversAfterBlackholedController 65/1 idle
./internal/app TestLabTLSHostSessionRecoversAfterControllerLoss 38/1 idle
./internal/app TestAuthenticatedOperatorToHostDeliveryWithControllerLoss 32/1 idle
./internal/app TestThree 20
./internal/app TestOne 12
./internal/app Test* 1
./internal/bootstrapstart TestStart 30
./internal/bootstrapstart TestRetry 4 norace
./tests/deploy TestOfflineReadbackMismatchDiscardsCandidate 300/60 solo
./tests/deploy * 10
`

type schedulerState struct {
	Active, Maximum         int
	IdleActive, IdleMaximum int
	CPUActive, CPUMaximum   int
	Commands                [][]string
	GORACE                  []string
}

set -euo pipefail
# wait -n -p needs bash 5.1; older shells would fail mid-suite with an
# unbound variable instead of this message.
((BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 5 || BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 5 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] >= 1)) \
	|| { echo "race-test.sh needs bash >= 5.1 (wait -n -p), not $BASH_VERSION" >&2; exit 2; }

# GO may be a command with arguments, such as "mise exec -- go".
read -r -a go <<< "${GO:-go}"
shards=${TS_RACE_SHARDS:-6}
# Uninstrumented tests are cheap; fewer shards avoid extra test binaries.
norace_shards=${TS_RACE_NORACE_SHARDS:-2}
jobs=${TS_RACE_JOBS:-6}
idle_jobs=${TS_RACE_IDLE_JOBS:-5}
package_jobs=${TS_RACE_PACKAGE_JOBS:-4}
test_jobs=${TS_RACE_TEST_JOBS:-2}
tier=${TS_TEST_TIER:-full}
durations=${TS_RACE_DURATIONS:-$(dirname -- "$(realpath -- "$0")")/race-durations.txt}
# The image contract suite drives the offline builder through hundreds of
# command fakes per test; unsharded it serialised most of the CI job.
sharded_packages=(./internal/app ./internal/bootstrapstart ./internal/natscell ./tests/deploy)
configured_packages=("${sharded_packages[@]}")
# Shard, listing and log names use the package's last element.
declare -A seen_base=()
for package in "${sharded_packages[@]}"; do
	[[ -z ${seen_base[${package##*/}]:-} ]] || { echo "sharded packages share the name ${package##*/}: $package" >&2; exit 2; }
	seen_base[${package##*/}]=1
done
[[ $shards =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_SHARDS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $norace_shards =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_NORACE_SHARDS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $jobs =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_JOBS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $idle_jobs =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_IDLE_JOBS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $package_jobs =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_PACKAGE_JOBS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $test_jobs =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'TS_RACE_TEST_JOBS must be a positive integer' >&2; exit 2; }
case $tier in
	pr) short=(-short) ;;
	full) short=() ;;
	*) echo 'TS_TEST_TIER must be pr or full' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[[ -f $durations && -r $durations ]] || { echo "race durations file is not readable: $durations" >&2; exit 2; }

# Every test binary and re-executed child skips the race runtime's default
# one-second exit sleep; the tests themselves wait for their goroutines.
export GORACE="${GORACE:+$GORACE }atexit_sleep_ms=0"

# Each line: <package> <test or glob> <seconds>[/<seconds under -short>]
# [cpu|solo|idle|norace], or "rest - <seconds>" for the shard of all other
# packages. The first matching line wins; unmatched tests cost one second.
entry_package=()
entry_test=()
entry_cost=()
entry_pool=()
rest_cost=1
line_number=0
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
	line_number=$((line_number + 1))
	line=${line%%#*}
	package='' test='' cost='' pool='' extra=''
	read -r package test cost pool extra <<< "$line" || true
	[[ -n $package ]] || continue
	pool=${pool:-cpu}
	# No leading zeros: arithmetic would read them as octal.
	[[ -n $test && $cost =~ ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(/(0|[1-9][0-9]*))?$ && $pool =~ ^(cpu|solo|idle|norace)$ && -z $extra ]] || {
		echo "$durations:$line_number: want <package> <test> <seconds>[/<short seconds>] [cpu|solo|idle|norace]" >&2
		exit 2
	}
	if [[ $tier == pr ]]; then cost=${cost#*/}; else cost=${cost%%/*}; fi
	if [[ $package == rest ]]; then
		rest_cost=$cost
		continue
	fi
	entry_package+=("$package")
	entry_test+=("$test")
	entry_cost+=("$cost")
	entry_pool+=("$pool")
done < "$durations"
estimate() {
	local i
	for i in "${!entry_package[@]}"; do
		# The test column is a glob pattern.
		# shellcheck disable=SC2053
		if [[ ${entry_package[i]} == "$1" && $2 == ${entry_test[i]} ]]; then
			est_cost=${entry_cost[i]}
			est_pool=${entry_pool[i]}
			matched[$i]=1
			return
		fi
	done
	est_cost=1
	est_pool=cpu
}

logs=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/race-test.XXXXXXXX")
declare -A active=() active_pool=()
running_cpu=0
running_idle=0
failed=0
# Invoked through the EXIT trap.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
cleanup() {
	local pid
	if ((${#active[@]})); then
		# Each shard leads its own process group (see start), so this also
		# stops its go test and test binary children, not just the subshell.
		for pid in "${!active[@]}"; do
			kill -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
		done
		wait || true
	fi
	rm -rf -- "$logs"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
finish() {
	local completed='' status rc=0 pid
	wait -n -p completed "${!active[@]}" || rc=$?
	if [[ -z $completed ]]; then
		# Some bash releases stop reporting a shard to wait -n once it has
		# already terminated and been marked notified (for example while
		# another shard's log was printed); wait -n then returns 127 without
		# a pid. A plain wait still returns such a shard's saved status.
		for pid in "${!active[@]}"; do
			if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
				completed=$pid
				rc=0
				wait "$pid" || rc=$?
				break
			fi
		done
		if [[ -z $completed ]]; then
			echo "race-test.sh: wait -n reported no finished shard (status $rc)" >&2
			exit 2
		fi
	fi
	if ((rc == 0)); then status=ok; else status=FAIL; failed=1; fi
	local name=${active[$completed]}
	if [[ ${active_pool[$completed]} == idle ]]; then
		running_idle=$((running_idle - 1))
	else
		running_cpu=$((running_cpu - 1))
	fi
	printf '=== race %s: %s\n' "$name" "$status"
	cat "$logs/$name.log"
	unset 'active[$completed]' 'active_pool[$completed]'
}
available() {
	if [[ $1 == idle ]]; then ((running_idle < idle_jobs)); else ((running_cpu < jobs)); fi
}
start() {
	local name=$1 pool=$2
	shift 2
	printf 'race start %s pool=%s\n' "$name" "$pool"
	# Job control gives the shard its own process group, so cleanup can stop
	# the whole tree after an abnormal exit.
	set -m
	(
		started=$SECONDS
		status=0
		"$@" || status=$?
		printf 'race %s elapsed=%ss\n' "$name" "$((SECONDS - started))"
		exit "$status"
	) > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1 &
	set +m
	active[$!]=$name
	active_pool[$!]=$pool
	if [[ $pool == idle ]]; then running_idle=$((running_idle + 1)); else running_cpu=$((running_cpu + 1)); fi
}

module=$("${go[@]}" list -m)
"${go[@]}" list ./... > "$logs/packages"
present=()
for package in "${sharded_packages[@]}"; do
	if grep -q -x -F -e "$module/${package#./}" "$logs/packages"; then
		present+=("$package")
		printf '%s\n' "$module/${package#./}"
	fi
done > "$logs/sharded"
sharded_packages=("${present[@]}")
mapfile -t other_packages < <(grep -v -x -F -f "$logs/sharded" "$logs/packages")
# Discover all shards before running tests: a failed listing must fail CI,
# and no package has several cold compilers/linkers running simultaneously.
for package in "${sharded_packages[@]}"; do
	if ! "${go[@]}" test -race -vet=off -list '.*' "$package" > "$logs/${package##*/}.list" 2>&1; then
		cat "$logs/${package##*/}.list" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
done

# Queue lines: <estimated seconds> <shard name> <pool> <package> <-run expression>.
tab=$'\t'
declare -A matched=()
: > "$logs/queue"
if ((${#other_packages[@]})); then
	printf '%s\tpackages\tcpu\t\t\n' "$rest_cost" >> "$logs/queue"
fi
# pack <package> <packed list> <shard name prefix> <pool> <shards>: longest processing
# time first, each test joins the shard with the least estimated work so
# far, or the fewest tests when estimates tie. Adds the packed tests to
# covered.
pack() {
	local package=$1 list=$2 prefix=$3 pool=$4 bins=$5 bin best cost test shard=0 expression
	local -a loads=() counts=() members=()
	for ((bin = 0; bin < bins; bin++)); do loads[bin]=0; counts[bin]=0; members[bin]=; done
	while read -r cost test; do
		best=0
		for ((bin = 1; bin < bins; bin++)); do
			if ((loads[bin] < loads[best] || (loads[bin] == loads[best] && counts[bin] < counts[best]))); then
				best=$bin
			fi
		done
		loads[best]=$((loads[best] + cost))
		counts[best]=$((counts[best] + 1))
		members[best]="${members[best]:+${members[best]}|}$test"
	done < <(LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1nr -k2,2 "$list")
	for ((bin = 0; bin < bins; bin++)); do
		[[ -n ${members[bin]} ]] || continue
		expression=$(tr '|' '\n' <<< "${members[bin]}" | LC_ALL=C sort | paste -s -d '|')
		covered=$((covered + $(tr '|' '\n' <<< "$expression" | wc -l)))
		printf '%s\t%s-%s\t%s\t%s\t^(%s)$\n' "${loads[bin]}" "$prefix" "$shard" "$pool" "$package" "$expression" >> "$logs/queue"
		shard=$((shard + 1))
	done
}
for package in "${sharded_packages[@]}"; do
	base=${package##*/}
	mapfile -t tests < <(grep -E '^(Test|Example|Fuzz)[A-Za-z0-9_]*$' "$logs/$base.list" | LC_ALL=C sort)
	((${#tests[@]} > 0)) || { echo "no tests listed in $package" >&2; exit 1; }
	: > "$logs/$base.packed"
	: > "$logs/$base.norace"
	covered=0
	for test in "${tests[@]}"; do
		estimate "$package" "$test"
		case $est_pool in
			cpu) printf '%s %s\n' "$est_cost" "$test" >> "$logs/$base.packed" ;;
			norace) printf '%s %s\n' "$est_cost" "$test" >> "$logs/$base.norace" ;;
			*)
				printf '%s\t%s-%s\t%s\t%s\t^(%s)$\n' "$est_cost" "$base" "$test" "${est_pool/solo/cpu}" "$package" "$test" >> "$logs/queue"
				covered=$((covered + 1))
				;;
		esac
	done
	pack "$package" "$logs/$base.packed" "$base" cpu "$shards"
	pack "$package" "$logs/$base.norace" "$base-norace" norace "$norace_shards"
	[[ $covered == "${#tests[@]}" ]] || { echo "shards of $package cover $covered of ${#tests[@]} tests" >&2; exit 1; }
done
mapfile -t queue < <(LC_ALL=C sort -t "$tab" -k1,1nr -k2,2 "$logs/queue")
printf 'race plan tier=%s cpu_jobs=%s idle_jobs=%s shards=%s\n' "$tier" "$jobs" "$idle_jobs" "${#queue[@]}"
for entry in "${queue[@]}"; do
	IFS="$tab" read -r cost name pool _ _ <<< "$entry"
	printf 'race queue %s pool=%s estimate=%ss\n' "$name" "$pool" "$cost"
done
# Estimates must stay live like every other input: an entry naming no
# sharded package can never apply, and a named test that matches no listed
# test (renamed, removed, or shadowed by an earlier line) has gone stale.
stale=0
for i in "${!entry_package[@]}"; do
	[[ -z ${matched[$i]:-} ]] || continue
	configured=0
	for package in "${configured_packages[@]}"; do
		[[ ${entry_package[i]} != "$package" ]] || configured=1
	done
	if ((!configured)); then
		printf 'race durations: %s is not a sharded package\n' "${entry_package[i]}" >&2
		stale=1
		continue
	fi
	in_module=0
	for package in "${sharded_packages[@]}"; do
		[[ ${entry_package[i]} != "$package" ]] || in_module=1
	done
	if ((in_module)) && [[ ${entry_test[i]} != *[*?[]* ]]; then
		printf 'race durations: %s %s matches no listed test\n' "${entry_package[i]}" "${entry_test[i]}" >&2
		stale=1
	fi
done
((!stale)) || exit 1
# Start the longest queued shard that has a free slot in its pool; a full
# CPU pool never holds back an idle lab, nor the other way round.
while ((${#queue[@]})); do
	next=
	for index in "${!queue[@]}"; do
		IFS="$tab" read -r _ name pool package expression <<< "${queue[index]}"
		if available "$pool"; then next=$index; break; fi
	done
	if [[ -z $next ]]; then finish; continue; fi
	unset 'queue[next]'
	if [[ -z $package ]]; then
		# Script contract packages invoke thousands of bounded subprocesses.
		# Under race instrumentation their aggregate can exceed Go's default
		# ten minutes.
		start "$name" "$pool" "${go[@]}" test -race -vet=off -timeout=20m "${short[@]}" -p "$package_jobs" -parallel "$test_jobs" "${other_packages[@]}"
	else
		race=(-race)
		[[ $pool != norace ]] || race=()
		start "$name" "$pool" "${go[@]}" test "${race[@]}" -vet=off -timeout=20m "${short[@]}" -parallel "$test_jobs" -run "$expression" "$package"
	fi
done

while ((${#active[@]})); do finish; done
exit "$failed"

spans.text:
logs=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/race-test.XXXXXXXX")
declare -A active=() active_pool=()
running_cpu=0
running_idle=0
failed=0
# Invoked through the EXIT trap.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
cleanup() {
	local pid
	if ((${#active[@]})); then
		# Each shard leads its own process group (see start), so this also
		# stops its go test and test binary children, not just the subshell.
		for pid in "${!active[@]}"; do
			kill -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
		done
		wait || true
	fi
	rm -rf -- "$logs"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
finish() {
	local completed='' status rc=0 pid
	wait -n -p completed "${!active[@]}" || rc=$?
	if [[ -z $completed ]]; then
		# Some bash releases stop reporting a shard to wait -n once it has
		# already terminated and been marked notified (for example while
		# another shard's log was printed); wait -n then returns 127 without
		# a pid. A plain wait still returns such a shard's saved status.
		for pid in "${!active[@]}"; do
			if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
				completed=$pid
				rc=0
				wait "$pid" || rc=$?
				break
			fi
		done
		if [[ -z $completed ]]; then
			echo "race-test.sh: wait -n reported no finished shard (status $rc)" >&2
			exit 2
		fi
	fi
	if ((rc == 0)); then status=ok; else status=FAIL; failed=1; fi
	local name=${active[$completed]}
	if [[ ${active_pool[$completed]} == idle ]]; then
		running_idle=$((running_idle - 1))
	else
		running_cpu=$((running_cpu - 1))
	fi
	printf '=== race %s: %s\n' "$name" "$status"
	cat "$logs/$name.log"
	unset 'active[$completed]' 'active_pool[$completed]'
}
available() {
	if [[ $1 == idle ]]; then ((running_idle < idle_jobs)); else ((running_cpu < jobs)); fi
}
start() {
	local name=$1 pool=$2
	shift 2
	printf 'race start %s pool=%s\n' "$name" "$pool"
	# Job control gives the shard its own process group, so cleanup can stop
	# the whole tree after an abnormal exit.
	set -m
	(
		started=$SECONDS
		status=0
		"$@" || status=$?
		printf 'race %s elapsed=%ss\n' "$name" "$((SECONDS - started))"
		exit "$status"
	) > "$logs/$name.log" 2>&1 &
	set +m
	active[$!]=$name
	active_pool[$!]=$pool
	if [[ $pool == idle ]]; then running_idle=$((running_idle + 1)); else running_cpu=$((running_cpu + 1)); fi
}

# Start the longest queued shard that has a free slot in its pool; a full
# CPU pool never holds back an idle lab, nor the other way round.
while ((${#queue[@]})); do
	next=
	for index in "${!queue[@]}"; do
		IFS="$tab" read -r _ name pool package expression <<< "${queue[index]}"
		if available "$pool"; then next=$index; break; fi
	done
	if [[ -z $next ]]; then finish; continue; fi
	unset 'queue[next]'
	if [[ -z $package ]]; then
		# Script contract packages invoke thousands of bounded subprocesses.
		# Under race instrumentation their aggregate can exceed Go's default
		# ten minutes.
		start "$name" "$pool" "${go[@]}" test -race -vet=off -timeout=20m "${short[@]}" -p "$package_jobs" -parallel "$test_jobs" "${other_packages[@]}"
	else
		race=(-race)
		[[ $pool != norace ]] || race=()
		start "$name" "$pool" "${go[@]}" test "${race[@]}" -vet=off -timeout=20m "${short[@]}" -parallel "$test_jobs" -run "$expression" "$package"
	fi
done

while ((${#active[@]})); do finish; done
exit "$failed"
